entries.hypothesis: Payload as an RSA signature/ciphertext under known Cicada moduli: compute `pow(s,e,n)` in both endiannesses for every published 3301 modulus and pattern-match PKCS#1 v1.5 / PSS structure. Zero-false-positive test, minutes of compute, never run. The ledger's "not a prime / modulus is even" result does not address it.
entries.threshold: Structural predicate, no tunable bar (round18/L5-payload/PREREG.md B.1/B.5, inherited unedited): HIT iff pow(s,e,n) carries PKCS#1 v1.5 type-1 (00 01 FF*k>=8 00 DigestInfo), v1.5 type-2 (00 02 PS>=8 00 msg) or EMSA-PSS (0xBC trailer, MGF1-unmasked DB = 00* || 01 || salt at a standard salt length) structure. No structure = null. C1 added one NEW pre-registered acceptance rule (round19/C1/PREREG.md 3.2): the control passes only if the matcher fires on a genuine signature AND recovers the true digest / message / salt length, AND scores ZERO false positives on 10,000 random blocks per modulus size.
entries.control_detail: Locally generated RSA-2048 and RSA-4096 keys, genuine signatures from `cryptography`. All 6 plants fire and are recovered exactly: v1.5 type-1 fires and its recovered DigestInfo is SHA-256 with the digest equal to the real SHA-256 of the signed message (both key sizes); EMSA-PSS fires and recovers salt_len 32 = the salt length used (both sizes); v1.5 type-2 fires and recovers the plaintext (both sizes). False positives on uniform random blocks: 0/10,000 at 2048-bit and 0/10,000 at 4096-bit across all three matchers - the pre-registered bar. An additional non-bar 100,000-block run measured 1 false positive at each size, both from the v1.5 type-2 matcher (1.0e-5 measured against an analytic ~1.5e-5), and ZERO from type-1 and PSS - i.e. the matchers' measured FP rate matches their analytic rate.
entries.null: PREREG B.1 H0: no structure. Not rejected.
entries.result: NEGATIVE (structural null, with the named Round 16 coverage gap closed). Round 16 recorded E-01 as coverage-limited because 'the 7A35090F RSA-4096 moduli (the correct size) were not on disk and not fetched'. Re-running round16/zeroFP/zerofp_tests.py shows what that actually amounted to: 1 modulus, 8 pow() checks, ALL EIGHT SKIPPED for s>=n - Round 16 evaluated ZERO modular exponentiations for E-01. The moduli were on disk all along, under ten witnesses including two keyserver pulls, and no network fetch was needed. Round 16's stated justification for not fetching them - 'under a 4096-bit modulus, pow(s,e,n) would trivially return s^e as-is (s << n), so PKCS1 padding is impossible' - is arithmetically false for every e > 1 (s is 2048-bit; s^3 is ~6144-bit and s^65537 is ~1.3e8 bits, both of which reduce mod a 4096-bit n). C1 ran the test: for the 3301 moduli, 54 (modulus x endianness x block alignment x exponent x payload variant) tuples evaluated and 36 arithmetically excluded because s >= n, ZERO structural matches. Broadened to every RSA public key on disk (22 distinct keys from 3,716 key-shaped files), 594 tuples evaluated, 144 excluded, ZERO structural matches. One arithmetic exclusion is itself informative: the payload's leading byte 0xcb exceeds the leading bytes of both 3301 moduli (0xc1 primary, 0xbc subkey), so the 256-byte payload placed in the HIGH half of a 4096-bit block is already too large to be a valid signature representative under either key - that placement is excluded by arithmetic, not merely untested. Independently replicated in the same wall-clock window by the concurrent round18/L5-payload run (different matcher implementation, different encoding enumeration, same verdict NULL and same skip pattern).
entries.coverage: Moduli: 3301's 7A35090F primary (4096-bit, e=65537, fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F) and its subkey (4096-bit, DEC57731ACCBFD11EEBA13434D390ECF671DDEB1), both fingerprinted from the OpenPGP packet body rather than from a filename, plus the 432-bit 2013 puzzle modulus, plus 20 further RSA public keys found by scanning all 3,716 key-shaped files under corpus/ and liber-primus/ (none of them 3301's; they are Round 18 L8's base-rate keys - Tor Browser devs, Tails, GnuPG release, bitcoin-core - and two solver-tool keys). Payload variants: canon_256.bin, canon_256_decpref.bin, payload_resolved.bin. Encodings: big-endian, little-endian (byte-reversed), and for moduli wider than the payload both left-aligned (zero-padded low) and right-aligned (zero-padded high) block placements. Exponents: 65537, 3, 17. Matchers: PKCS#1 v1.5 type 1 with DigestInfo for MD5/SHA-1/224/256/384/512, PKCS#1 v1.5 type 2, EMSA-PSS under MGF1-SHA-1/256/384/512 at salt lengths {0,20,28,32,48,64,hLen}. 738 tuples enumerated in total.
entries.not_covered: (a) RSA moduli 3301 never published - in particular the moduli behind the three 2014 onion RSA blobs, which are encrypted MESSAGES (ciphertexts), not public keys, so their n is not recoverable from what is on disk. (b) The 432-bit 2013 modulus as a signing key over a 54-byte WINDOW of the payload rather than the whole 256 bytes - all 18 of its tuples are excluded by s >= n and no windowing was pre-registered. (c) Blinded signatures, partially-known signatures, and any signature of which the payload is a fragment. (d) OAEP and raw unpadded RSA. (e) Any payload transform outside the four enumerated integer encodings (e.g. bit-reversed, hex-ASCII, or a re-ordered byte permutation). (f) e outside {65537, 3, 17}.

entries.notes: Provenance nit worth keeping: corpus/A-primary-artifacts/ibotpeaches/keys/67F363C61BA8FB6FDBA9C47D0670B0E57A35090F.asc is MISNAMED - the key inside it fingerprints as 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F.
